properties.disease overview: Traumatic loss of congruency of the glenohumeral joint. Anterior dislocation is most common (≈90–95%) and typically occurs with the arm abducted and externally rotated or after FOOSH. Posterior dislocation is uncommon and classically associated with seizures or electric shock.
properties.mechanism: High-energy force drives the humeral head out of the glenoid. Anterior dislocation often produces Bankart lesion (anterior labrum injury) and Hill-Sachs lesion (humeral head impaction defect). Neurovascular compromise—especially axillary nerve injury—must be assessed; older patients should be assessed for rotator cuff tear after dislocation.
